step1_analysis.description: A single-ended transimpedance pre-amplifier utilizing a common-emitter (mapped to common-source in CMOS) stage with shunt-shunt feedback and an emitter-follower (source-follower) output buffer. It is designed to convert an input current from a photodiode into an output voltage with high bandwidth.

paper_reference.title: 40-GHz Transimpedance Amplifier With Differential Outputs Using InP–InGaAs Heterojunction Bipolar Transistors

sky130_expected.calculation: Zt ≈ Rf. With Rf = 1kOhm, Zt = 20*log10(1000) = 60 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined primarily by the feedback resistor Rf. Adjusted to 1kOhm for stable operation in 130nm CMOS.

sky130_expected.calculation: f_3db ≈ 1 / (2*pi*Rf*Cin). Assuming Cin ~ 50fF and Rf = 1kOhm, f_3db ≈ 3.18 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: SKY130 130nm CMOS is significantly slower than InP HBTs; expected bandwidth is in the low GHz range rather than 40 GHz.
Scaled down for 1.8V supply and typical CMOS bias currents compared to the original 4V HBT design.
